title: Colonial America
examples: What were the main differences between the northern and southern colonies?
How did the economy of the colonies change over time?
Can you explain the role of different groups in the colonial economy?

explain.say: Today we learn about the colonies in America. These were areas settled by Britain. They developed unique ways of life. We will look at how they were organized.
The colonies were grouped into regions. The New England colonies were known for trade. They had many small towns and fishing.
The Middle colonies had a diverse population. They were known for farming and varied crops. This made them quite different.
The Southern colonies focused on large plantations. Their economy relied heavily on cash crops. Tobacco and rice were important.
Economies in the colonies were based on exports. They grew crops or goods to sell overseas. This was their main source of wealth.
Think about the economy of a modern city. Local businesses sell goods to people from all over. This is like the colonial trade routes.

faq.q: Why did the different regions develop different economies?
faq.a: The environment and the available resources shaped what people could grow or trade. For example, the climate was different in the north versus the south.

faq.q: Were all the colonies equal in their economies?
faq.a: No, the economies varied greatly. The southern colonies focused on large-scale agriculture, while the northern ones focused on smaller trades.
asks: Did all colonies make the same money?
What was the biggest economic difference between colonies?

faq.q: What were the main cash crops in the South?
faq.a: The most important cash crops were tobacco and rice. These were grown for profit to be shipped back to Britain.

faq.q: What was the role of trade in the North?
faq.a: Trade was very important in the North. People used the rivers and coastline for fishing and buying goods from other places.
asks: How did the North make money?
What did New England focus on?

faq.q: Did the people work on plantations or in shops?
faq.a: It depended on the region. Plantation work was common in the South, but skilled trades like carpentry were common in the North.
asks: What kind of labor was common?

facts: The New England colonies focused on fishing and shipbuilding.
The Southern colonies relied on large plantations and cash crops.
The Middle colonies had a mix of farming and trade goods.
Colonial economies were heavily connected to trade with Britain.

quiz.say: Which region focused on crops like tobacco and rice?
quiz.why: The South's warm climate was perfect for growing these cash crops.

wrong.0: The environment caused very different economic focuses.
wrong.2: They focused more on fishing and small-scale trade.
wrong.3: They were more diverse, not specialized in one cash crop.

quiz.say: If a colony sold goods to another country, what was this process?
quiz.why: Sending goods out to be sold in another place is called exporting.

wrong.0: This means making everything without outside help.
wrong.2: Importing means bringing goods into the colony.
wrong.3: Bartering is trading one item directly for another item.

quiz.say: Which area was known for its diverse mix of farming and trade?
quiz.why: The Middle Colonies had a variety of resources allowing for diverse economies.

wrong.1: Their economy was more specialized towards maritime activities.
wrong.2: Their economy was dominated by large plantations.
wrong.3: The Middle Colonies were known for both farming and trade.
